title: Evaluating Large Language Models’ Responses to Sexual and Reproductive Health Queries in Nepali

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating language consistency by tracking whether the model defaults to a high-resource language (English) when prompted in a low-resource language (Nepali), and comparing response accuracy and quality across Devanagari script, Romanized Nepali, and English.

Human expert annotation using the LEAF framework to assess 'Cultural appropriateness,' determining if the generated responses align with the local Nepali culture and context (e.g., suggesting medical products actually available in the local market).

Human expert evaluation under the 'Sensitivity' criterion of the LEAF framework to flag responses containing ethical concerns, broad social biases, insensitivity, or inappropriate/obscene language that harms the dignity of an individual or community.
